speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry will consider enfolding all Special Education school teachers to come under the Ministry so that they will be able to receive the benefits of being an MOE teacher; and (b) if not, whether there are any future plans to do so to help attract and retain talent in this sector.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what is the current status of the supply and readiness of Special Education teachers to meet Singapore’s needs in the next five years; and (b) what plans does the Ministry have to attract talent to join the special education sector and to retain them in the profession.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, in Singapore, Special Education (SPED) is supported by the Government, community funders and Social Service Agencies (SSAs).

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The SSAs have been delivering special education for children with moderate-to-severe special educational needs for decades.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: While full funding is provided for SPED, SSAs today retain substantial autonomy, including the hiring of staff for their respective SPED schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE has been working closely and supporting SSAs to enhance the career proposition and professionalism of SPED teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: One major HR initiative, done in consultation and partnership with SSAs, was the Journeys of Excellence Package, in short, the Journeys Package, launched in 2020.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Journeys Package aims to strengthen the professionalism in SPED as well as recognise the years of experience and service of many SPED educators by placing them at the appropriate competency levels and raising the job size of senior SPED teachers to more closely align with those of equivalent MOE teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE has been working with SPED schools to put in place progressive HR frameworks to support teacher retention and career development, taking a leaf from MOE’s own frameworks.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: One example is increasing the number of key personnel positions in SPED schools to provide career advancement opportunities for good-performing SPED teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To receive the second funding tranche, SPED schools will need to implement more progressive HR practices and the corresponding increases in SPED teacher salaries.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: SPED schools will determine the salary adjustments for their teachers at different levels based on performance and current salary structures.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Around seven in 10 SPED teachers have obtained DISE or joined the sector with other recognised teaching credentials.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For the remaining 500 teachers, around half are either on the current course or will be enrolled in DISE in January 2023.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE also funds in-service training for SPED teachers and invites SPED teachers teaching the national curriculum to attend in-service training alongside MOE teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In addition, MOE offers Masters Scholarships in Special Education tenable either overseas or locally.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE also works with partners to recognise and profile the important work of SPED teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Outstanding SPED Teacher Award and the soon-to-be-implemented Promising SPED Teacher Award by MOE and SG Enable seek to identify and honour exemplary SPED teachers who are impactful and good role models in the fraternity.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In addition, MOE has seconded MOE educators who have the passion to serve as teachers and key personnel in SPED schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This includes seconding experienced MOE educators to serve as SPED school principals and vice principals, upon the SSAs’ request.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Currently, there are 14 principals and vice principals who are MOE-secondees out of a total of 47 SPED school leaders.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE is committed to partner closely the SSAs in this journey towards professionalism.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, I am prepared to work with my staff, SSAs and the community to explore different and new models.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I would set out five conditions for us to consider as to whether a new model is better and more appropriate.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, the new model, if it comes about, must deliver better outcomes for our SPED children.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Second, the new model, if it comes about, must deliver better outcomes in terms of support for the SPED children's family.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Third, the model must provide better training opportunities and professional development for our SPED teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Fourth, the model must be able to engage the community to participate and partake in the endeavour.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Fifth, we must also have a model that allows a better continuum of care and support from preschool to school and the post-school environment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we are prepared to explore new models with SSAs and the community, so long as we bear in mind these five criteria that I have just laid out.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will be happy to have this conversation with the SSAs and our community partners on how we can take the SPED education sector forward as part of our Forward SG exercise.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I am very heartened to hear that they are ready to work with the relevant SSAs and organisations.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: They are still represented by the Singapore Manual & Mercantile Workers' Union – I understand it maybe because they may have been better adapted to handle this.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: How has that changed moving forward, so that MOE can better work with the SPED organisations and SPED individuals in this current moment to help retain and attract more SPED teachers to this vocation?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I shall not attempt to answer on behalf of NTUC, but as the ex-Secretary-General of NTUC, I will say that I will leave it to NTUC to decide which union best serves the interests of the SPED school teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE is agnostic, regardless of whether the SPED school teachers are with SMMWU, STU or any of the other teachers' unions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE will continue to work closely with them and also with their SSA organisations.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I just want to ask the Minister to consider that the whole special education model does not comprise only of staff who are known as teachers.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Actually, the holistic development of our students over in the SPED system especially, really includes individuals like the allied professionals, psychologists, therapists, occupational therapists (OTs), speech pathologists, social workers and other staff.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, in considering and even publicising decisions on salaries and benefits packages of mainstream and other SPED school teachers, we need to consider that the other staff also play critical roles and to also include them as we design future models and future compensation packages for them.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: But my Question No 6 is about whether we are right now meeting the targets of having enough teachers come forward to enter the SPED sector.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So, is there any kind of operational disconnect for SSAs that they have to navigate, because of this dual Ministry involvement in terms of the development of the sector?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, I think we have to deal with the quantity and quality of manpower; two, we have to deal with the pain points that the Member mentioned; and three, it has to do with the organisational structures that we have to deal with.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the first issue, on the quantity and quality of manpower, certainly, we would need to do much more to increase the number of SPED school educators and support staff.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I must share this with the House.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In planning for a SPED school, the manpower needs are not as straightforward as a conventional school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because in a conventional school, the needs are perhaps more homogeneous whereas, in a SPED school, different SPED children have different types of needs and different degrees of severity.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is why the planning is not as straightforward.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do have certain planning ratios, but we, certainly, will need and would like to recruit more Singaporeans to join the SPED sector.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second issue is about the pain points.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For many of us who have SPED children or have been involved in the SPED school sector, we would know that it is emotionally very demanding.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I have given guidance to my staff that we cannot just plan on the basis of how many staff we need for how many children.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We need to have a bit of a buffer, if you would like, for us to be able to roster our people to go for training and also, sometimes, for them to take a break.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, that is one part of how we try to address the pain points.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second part is that we would also like to have a wider group of people who understand the SPED community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Even within the MOE conventional schools, we have our fair share of some special needs children where we would need to "up" the skills level of many of our teachers to take care of the higher needs of these children in our conventional schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is why we have a system to roster some of our teachers to the SPED schools to cross-share experiences, so that we can take better care of the SPED children in our conventional schools and yet, at the same time, allow some of the SPED school teachers some time to go for their own training and perhaps to be rostered out for a break in their long journey with the SPED sector.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, these are, indeed, some of the things that we need to do.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the third point about the structure and organisations, rest assured that the two of us work closely together.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have this model before and we started this model between MSF and MOE, not just for SPED, but we did this for early childhood education.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: ECDA is an agency that jointly reports to Minister Masagos and myself.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And, of course, I have a secret weapon, to make sure that nothing falls between the cracks.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: She is both the Permanent Secretary in MOE and MSF.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I have personally asked her to oversee the continuum to work out the models required to support our SPED community in terms of infrastructure and manpower.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I would say that between infrastructure and manpower, infrastructure is the easier of the two.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The more difficult of the two is for us to recruit the number and quality of people.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, we are both working closely now to deal with the most difficult challenge which we want to take a crack at and which we think we need to do much better at as a society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is the continuum of care from preschool to school and the post-18-year-olds' care and work arrangement for our SPED community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If anybody can do this well, it must be Singapore, because when the SPED children come to us in the preschools, we have the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC); we have the SPED schools for them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: With the data that is available, it enables MOE to forward plan the school system requirement.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And from MOE's data, we should be able to forward-plan the post-18 requirement and we really want to do this much better.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our current gap, the biggest gap, in my view, is not so much the preschool and the school system in which we have invested a lot of effort over the years; we can still do better.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just a quick question for the Minister in regard to his original reply where he stated that there were 1,600 SPED teachers, if I heard him correctly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I just confirm with the Minister whether that number includes the allied educators, who are an integral part of the SPED system?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: As the Minister also shared, in certain cases where there is a gap, a cognitive gap for certain children, the allied educator could be as, if not more important than the SPED teacher, depending on where the child is developmentally.
